directions.name: Thermal Camera UI
directions.thesis: The dashboard is a FLIR-style thermal imager: false-color isotherms, measurement crosshairs, and a calibrated scale bar make the heat decision visible before you read it.
directions.lineage: FLIR, Seek Thermal, industrial IR cameras — the tool supervisors already associate with 'seeing heat'
directions.type: Monospace telemetry (JetBrains Mono) + condensed UI labels (Space Grotesk)
directions.composition: Map occupies 60% viewport as the thermal view; decision card is a side panel reading like an on-screen display (OSD)
directions.topology: Single view: thermal map + OSD panel. No tabs. State lives in the reticle position and isotherm threshold
directions.controls: Threshold slider = isotherm level. Evaluate = capture frame. History = frame buffer
directions.states: LIVE (streaming), CAPTURED (decision frozen), ALARM (isotherm breached = RESCHEDULE)
directions.viewport: Dark thermal map fills left 60%; right panel shows decision in OSD layout: large decision badge, temperature readouts as digital displays, recommendation as scrolling telemetry line
directions.risk: Reads as a visualization tool, not a decision tool, if the OSD panel lacks authority. The decision must feel like the instrument's output, not a sidebar.

directions.name: Surveyor's Total Station
directions.thesis: The dashboard is a precision surveying instrument: clean grid, monospace angular readouts, hierarchical data density — every pixel serves the measurement.
directions.lineage: Leica, Trimble, Topcon total stations — the instrument supervisors respect for 'this is where the line goes'
directions.materials: matte charcoal ground, fine hairline grid, cyan/amber measurement text, subtle elevation contours
directions.type: Monospace for all measurements (JetBrains Mono), UI labels in Space Grotesk at 11px
directions.composition: Three-panel layout: map (theodolite view), measurement panel (angle/distance readouts), decision panel (the stake)
directions.topology: Instrument mode selector: SURVEY (map), MEASURE (temps), STAKE (decision). One active at a time.
directions.controls: Mode knob (3 positions). Enter key = accept measurement. Fn keys = quick actions
directions.states: READY, MEASURING, STAKED (decision locked), ERROR (no signal)
directions.viewport: Center: map with crosshair and bearing rings. Right: stacked readout panels — Site ID, Climate Zone, Peak/Avg Temp, Decision (large), Recommendation. Bottom: status bar with satellite count, battery, time
directions.risk: Can feel too sparse for a dashboard that needs to show reasoning text. The recommendation/reason fields need breathing room without breaking the instrument density.

directions.name: Industrial HMI/SCADA Panel
directions.thesis: The dashboard is a factory-floor operator interface: high-contrast dark mode, tag-based navigation, alarm banners, real-time trend sparks — built for glanceability at 3m in harsh light.
directions.lineage: Ignition, Wonderware, FactoryTalk, Siemens WinCC — the screens operators trust to shut down a line
directions.materials: Pure black ground, neon green (normal), amber (warning), red (alarm), yellow (caution), 1px white hairlines
directions.type: Roboto Mono for tags/values, Inter for labels — high legibility at distance
directions.composition: Header: site tag + time + alarm banner. Left: navigation tree (sites/zones). Center: graphic display (map + trend sparklines). Right: faceplate (decision detail)
directions.topology: Tag browser → graphic display → faceplate. Standard ISA-101 hierarchy.
directions.controls: Tag search (type-ahead). Acknowledge button on alarms. Trend time-range picker
directions.viewport: Full-bleed dark panel. Top 60px: site breadcrumb + live clock + alarm strip. Map with animated trend sparklines on hover. Decision faceplate slides in from right on evaluation: large status indicator, numeric tags, memo field for recommendation
directions.risk: Can feel like 'monitoring' not 'deciding'. The PROCEED/MODIFY/RESCHEDULE call must be the primary visual event, not one tag among many.

directions.name: Aviation EFIS (Glass Cockpit)
directions.thesis: The dashboard is a primary flight display: attitude tape metaphor for risk, vertical speed tape for temperature trend, alert hierarchy pilots trust with their lives — go/no-go is a flight directive.
directions.lineage: Garmin G1000/G3000, Honeywell Primus Epic, Collins Pro Line Fusion — where 'continue' vs 'divert' is a certified decision
directions.materials: Deep aviation blue ground, cyan/magenta/amber tapes, red warning flash, green safe arc
directions.type: Roboto Condensed for tape labels, Roboto Mono for digital readouts, Noto Sans for messages
directions.composition: Left: attitude-style risk indicator (artificial horizon = risk level). Center: map as moving map. Right: vertical tapes (temp trend, time to threshold). Bottom: message advisory bar
directions.topology: PFD (Primary Flight Display) + MFD (Multi-Function Display) split. Soft keys at bottom
directions.controls: Soft keys: EVAL, HIST, SETUP, ALERT. Range knob (time window). Baro knob (threshold adjust — locked in our case)
directions.states: NORMAL (green arcs), CAUTION (amber arcs), WARNING (red flash + aural), ADVISORY (white text)
directions.viewport: Landscape split: left 40% risk attitude indicator (large, unmistakable). Center 35% moving map with AOI ring. Right 25% vertical temperature tape + decision directive banner across bottom: 'CONTINUE OPERATION' / 'MODIFY OPERATION' / 'DIVERT — RESCHEDULE'
directions.risk: Aviation metaphor may feel alien to construction supervisors. The 'divert' language must map clearly to RESCHEDULE without requiring domain knowledge.

directions.name: Marine Chartplotter/Sonar
directions.thesis: The dashboard is a chartplotter with sonar split: dark water ground, precise waypoints, contour lines, track recording — the site is a waypoint, the AOI is a contour, the decision is a course change.
directions.lineage: Garmin GPSMAP, Raymarine Axiom, Simrad NSS, Furuno NavNet — where 'mark waypoint' and 'alter course' are muscle memory
directions.materials: Dark teal/black ground, contour lines, waypoint symbols, track line, sonar waterfall palette
directions.type: DM Sans for UI, JetBrains Mono for coordinates/depths, Outfit for alerts
directions.composition: Chart view (map) + sonar pane (temperature waterfall) + data boxes (waypoint info). Split adjustable.
directions.topology: Chart → Sonar → Data boxes. Waypoint list = history. Route = evaluation sequence.
directions.controls: MOB (Man Overboard) = emergency evaluate. Waypoint entry = search location. Route = scheduled evaluations
directions.states: NAVIGATING (live), WAYPOINT MARKED (evaluated), ALARM (shallow/heat), ANCHOR (decision locked)
directions.viewport: Chart view dominant. Sonar pane (bottom 30%) shows temperature waterfall scrolling right-to-left. Data boxes on right: Site (waypoint), Climate Zone (chart datum), Peak/Avg (depth soundings), Decision (course instruction). 'ALTER COURSE' banner on RESCHEDULE
directions.risk: Marine metaphor (waypoints, contours, course) needs clear mapping to construction language. 'Alter course' = RESCHEDULE must be instant.

directions.name: Scientific Field Instrument
directions.thesis: The dashboard is a rugged handheld datalogger: readable in direct sun, glove-friendly targets, battery/state bar, timestamped logs — the tool you tape to a tripod and trust.
directions.lineage: Campbell Scientific, Onset HOBO, Kestrel, Vaisala — instruments field scientists stake their data on
directions.materials: Dark charcoal, high-contrast text, colored status LEDs (virtual), tactile button metaphors
directions.type: IBM Plex Mono for readings, IBM Plex Sans for labels — legible at arm's length in sun
directions.composition: Full-screen card stack. One card at a time: SITE → CONDITIONS → DECISION → LOG. Swipe/keys to advance
directions.topology: Linear workflow wizard. Back = previous card. Home = site selector. Power = mock mode toggle
directions.controls: Large tactile buttons: [EVALUATE] [HISTORY] [SETTINGS]. Rotary encoder metaphor for time window
directions.states: IDLE, ACQUIRING (spinner), READY (decision shown), LOGGING (saved), LOW BATTERY (mock mode)
directions.viewport: Portrait-first card. Top: site name + climate zone badge + GPS fix quality. Middle: large temperature readouts (peak/avg) with threshold markers. Bottom: DECISION badge (full width, thumb-target). Swipe up for recommendation/reason. Swipe down for history
directions.risk: Portrait card stack works on phone but wastes desktop. Must adapt to landscape: side-by-side cards or persistent three-panel on wide screens.

directions.name: Mission Control Console
directions.thesis: The dashboard is a flight director's console: event timeline, telemetry strips, anomaly flags, voice-loop metaphor — the PROCEED/MODIFY/RESCHEDULE call is a GO/NO-GO poll with authority.
directions.lineage: NASA MCC, SpaceX Hawthorne, ESA ESOC — where 'Go for launch' is a recorded, defensible decision by named officers
directions.materials: Deep space black, console gray panels, amber event markers, green GO / red NO-GO / amber HOLD, monospace telemetry
directions.type: JetBrains Mono for all telemetry, IBM Plex Sans for officer labels, Space Grotesk for headers
directions.composition: Three horizontal bands: TOP — timeline (event log). MIDDLE — telemetry strips (map + temp trend + climate zone). BOTTOM — decision poll (the GO/NO-GO moment)
directions.topology: Console positions: FLIGHT (map), SURGEON (temps), CAPCOM (decision), SURGEON (climate). Each position has its strip
directions.controls: POLL button (evaluate). ACK (acknowledge alert). LOG (save). VOICE LOOP (Slack webhook metaphor)
directions.states: STANDBY, POLLING (acquiring), GO (PROCEED), HOLD (MODIFY), NO-GO (RESCHEDULE), ABORT (error)
directions.viewport: Landscape console. Top 20%: event timeline (horizontal, newest right). Middle 60%: three vertical strips — LEFT: map with AOI, CENTER: temperature trend sparkline with threshold bands, RIGHT: climate zone + thresholds. Bottom 20%: DECISION POLL — large GO/HOLD/NO-GO buttons, officer ID (supervisor name), timestamp, voice loop indicator (Slack). Recommendation/reason in CAPCOM strip
directions.risk: The console density can overwhelm. The decision poll must be the visual climax — everything else supports it. Mobile requires collapsing to single-strip scroll.
